slides.title: The 40% rule for ducts
slides.sub: Fill ratio and jam ratio, worked through

slides.title: Too full and the pull jams. Too big and you overpaid.
slides.body: Five minutes of arithmetic avoids both.

slides.title: Fill ratio, defined
slides.body: Total cable cross-section area divided by the duct's inside area. Planning limit for three or more cables: 40%.

slides.title: Where 40% comes from
slides.body: NEC Chapter 9 allows 53% for one cable, 31% for two, 40% for three or more. Telecom borrowed the rule.

slides.title: Use the real bore
slides.body: Take the inside diameter from the data sheet. A two-inch duct does not have a two-inch bore.

slides.title: Watch the jam ratio
slides.body: Duct inside diameter divided by cable diameter. Between 2.8 and 3.2, three cables can wedge side by side in a bend.

slides.title: Low fill, still jammed
slides.body: Three 0.5 inch cables in a 1.5 inch bore: ratio 3.0, fill only 33%. Squarely in the jam zone.

slides.title: Size a duct in 5 steps
items: Divide by the real inside area
Three cables? Check the jam ratio

slides.title: Save this for your next duct calculation

caption:
A duct can be only 33% full and still jam solid. The fill ratio is only half the check.

The other half is the jam ratio: three similar cables can wedge side by side in a bend when the duct is about three times their diameter. Swipe for both calculations and a worked example.
